To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the story of the creation and fall of man in Genesis 2 and 3 was created by combining two independent myths, one about the origin of man and the other about the origin of the monarchy.

the creation of man in Genesis is a composite story that is based upon the creation of the king in the ancient Near East, and that the creation of the man in Gen 2:7, the creation of the woman in Gen 2 :21, and the expulsion from Eden in Gen 3:23 24 are all based upon the creation and installation of the king in ancient Mesopotamia and Egypt.
The creation of man is not a single myth but rather a complex literary composition which has undergone a long and varied history of development.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single, or even a few, literary sources for the Genesis story, nor is there one single mythic tradition that lies behind it.

Gen 2 2 3 does not present a coherent account of the origin of man and his relation to God but is rather a compilation of several traditions which have been woven together in an artificial manner to form a single narrative.

the creation of man and the creation of the king in Genesis 2 3 are not two separate and unrelated accounts, but rather two sides of a single literary composition, which is an integral part of the larger story of the creation and fall of man in the Garden of Paradise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Creation of Man and the Creation of the King are parallel accounts of the creation of the first man, the first king, and their relationship to the divine king.
the creation of man in the Garden of Paradise is a story which has been constructed from a variety of elements which have been combined into a single story.
